\section*{TOAS papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS17-P1-PHY-S3-Q04, source={TOAS - Test 17 (18 Sep 2022)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Properties}, answer={50.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: electromagnetic wave force on a charge | steps: fields at the origin at that time; magnetic field from E/c; force on the charge; acceleration}]
A charged particle of charge 1$\mu$C and mass $10^{-6}$ kg is moving with a velocity of $9\times10^7\left(\hat i+2\hat k\right)$ m/s in space. There is a plane electromagnetic wave given by $\vec E=10^2\text{N/C}\,\hat i\sin(2\pi z-\omega t)$. The charge crosses origin at $t=\dfrac56$ns. At that moment, the magnitude of its acceleration is \underline{\hspace{1cm}} m/s$^2$ (Neglect relativistic effects)
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS17-P2-PHY-S1-Q10, source={TOAS - Test 17 (18 Sep 2022)}, paper=2, qno=10, type=single, subtopic={Properties}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S2 I0 C0 F0}, diff_note={concepts: intensity of an electromagnetic wave | steps: intensity from power and distance; amplitude of the electric field; magnetic field}]
The antenna of a 6 kW radio station radiates spherical wavefronts. At a distance of 100 m from the antenna, what is the peak magnetic field strength ?
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{20 nT}
\opt{B}{$10\sqrt2$nT}
\opt{C}{10nT}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac5{\sqrt2}$nT}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS18-P1-PHY-S3-Q01, source={TOAS - Test 18 (30 Oct 2022)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=numerical, subtopic={Properties}, answer={2}, answer_src=solved, working={A reflecting sphere (specular) feels the same force as an absorbing one, $F=I\pi R^2/c$, so $P/Q=1/1$ and $P+Q=2$}, difficulty=3, diff_parts={K1 S1 I1 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: radiation force on a sphere | steps: specular reflection from a sphere gives the same force as absorption; evaluate}]
Parallel beam of intensity $I$ incident on a sphere, which absorb 50\% of incident light and reflect remaining light. If radius of sphere is $R$ then radiation force on sphere is given by $\dfrac PQ\,\dfrac{I\left(\pi R^2\right)}c$ then $P+Q$ is (where $P$ and $Q$ are smallest possible natural number) :-
\end{bankq}

\section*{TNAS papers}
\begin{bankpassage}[id=TNAS06-P2-PHY-S3-G3-4, source={TNAS - Test 06 (30 Jul 2023)}, questions={3-4}]
The electric fields of two plane electromagnetic plane waves in vacuum are given by\par
$\vec E_1=E_{0}\hat j\cos(\omega t-kx)$ and $\vec E_2=E_0\hat k\cos(\omega t-ky)$\par
At $t=0$, a particle of charge $q$ is at origin moving with a velocity $\vec v=0.75c\,\hat j$. $c$ is the speed of light.
\end{bankpassage}

\begin{bankq}[id=TNAS06-P2-PHY-S3-Q04, source={TNAS - Test 06 (30 Jul 2023)}, paper=2, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Properties}, answer={1.25}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K1 S3 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: force on a charge in two electromagnetic waves | steps: fields at the origin; electric forces; magnetic forces for each wave; combine components; read a b c; sum}, group=TNAS06-P2-PHY-S3-G3-4]

\begin{bankq}[id=TNAS07-P1-PHY-S1-Q17, source={TNAS - Test 07 (20 Aug 2023)}, paper=1, qno=17, type=single, subtopic={Properties}, answer={C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: radiation pressure on a reflecting sail | steps: intensity at distance r; force on a perfect reflector; acceleration}]

One idea is to build a boat (mass $=m$) with large canvas (area $A$) and accelerate boat by radiation force exerted by solar radiation. \opt{B}{$\dfrac{PAc}{4\pi r^2m}$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{PA}{2\pi r^2cm}$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{PAc}{2\pi r^2m}$}

\begin{bankq}[id=TNAS07-P1-PHY-S2-Q01, source={TNAS - Test 07 (20 Aug 2023)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=numerical, subtopic={Properties}, answer={4}, answer_src=solved, working={Average energy density $=\tfrac12\varepsilon_0E_0^2=\tfrac12(8.85\times10^{-12})(100)=4.4\times10^{-10}$ J/m$^3$}, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: energy density of an electromagnetic wave | steps: electric and magnetic energy equal; average energy density; evaluate}]

\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TNAS07-P1-PHY-S2-Q02, source={TNAS - Test 07 (20 Aug 2023)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=numerical, subtopic={Properties}, answer={30}, answer_src=solved, working={$\vec k\propto(3,0,\sqrt3)$ so $\sin\theta_i=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{12}}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}2$, $\theta_i=60^\circ$; $\sin\theta_t=\dfrac{\sin60^\circ}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac12$, so $30^\circ$}, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: refraction of a plane electromagnetic wave | steps: wave vector components; angle of incidence; refractive index of the slab; Snell law}]

The angle of transmission in the dielectric slab Is \underline{\hspace{1cm}} degrees
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TNAS07-P1-PHY-S2-Q10, source={TNAS - Test 07 (20 Aug 2023)}, paper=1, qno=10, type=numerical, subtopic={Properties}, answer={1}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: transmission of an electromagnetic wave at an interface | steps: refractive indices; Fresnel amplitude relation; evaluate}]
